candidates: In xychart spec and parser test files, format multi-line diagram strings inside template literals with minimal, consistent indentation (ideally flush to the left margin or a single shallow indent level) so the diagram syntax is human-readable without visually misleading extra whitespace. Prefer placing the opening backtick on the same line as the call argument rather than starting on the next line.

When no explicit y-axis range is configured for an xychart with multiple bar datasets, the auto-computed lower bound must include an appropriate baseline (typically 0), not just the raw minimum of individual data values. An incorrect lower bound causes stacked bars to overflow the chart canvas. Audit the min/max derivation logic in `xychartDb.ts` to confirm the lower bound is anchored correctly for multi-dataset charts.

When computing the y-axis upper bound for a stacked bar xychart with multiple datasets, the maximum must be the largest *per-column sum* — i.e., for each x-position, sum the values of all datasets at that position, then take the max across positions. Using the global maximum of individual values or the total sum of all values across all positions will produce an incorrect (too high or too low) axis ceiling. Verify this column-wise aggregation in `xychartDb.ts`.
